findings.title: No lock_timeout before locking DDL
findings.why: If a long query holds a lock on orders, this statement waits for it, and every query that arrives afterwards queues behind this statement.

statement.sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN user_id bigint REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

fix.summary: Set a lock timeout at the top of the migration, and retry the migration if it times out:

findings.title: Foreign key blocks writes on "orders" and "users"
findings.why: Postgres checks every existing row of orders against users while it holds locks on both tables. INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on either table wait until the check finishes.

statement.sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN user_id bigint REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

fix.summary: Add the constraint as NOT VALID, then validate it in a separate transaction:

steps.title: Add the column and the constraint without checking existing rows
steps.code:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN user_id bigint;
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE NOT VALID;

steps.title: Validate it in a separate migration
steps.code: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_user_id_fkey;

findings.title: SET NOT NULL on "orders.status" blocks reads and writes during a full table scan
findings.why: Postgres scans all of orders to check for NULL values while it holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Every query on the table waits for the scan.

statement.sql: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN status SET NOT NULL

fix.summary: Prove the column has no NULL values with a CHECK constraint first, so SET NOT NULL skips the scan:

steps.title: Add the check without scanning existing rows
steps.code: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_status_not_null CHECK (status IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;

steps.title: Validate it in a separate migration
steps.code: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_status_not_null;

steps.title: Set NOT NULL, then drop the check
steps.code:
ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN status SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_status_not_null;

findings.title: Changing the type of "orders.user_id" rewrites the table
findings.why: Postgres rewrites every row of orders and rebuilds its indexes while it holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Reads and writes wait until the rewrite finishes.

statement.sql:
ALTER TABLE orders
  ALTER COLUMN user_id TYPE bigint,
  ALTER COLUMN external_id TYPE uuid USING external_id::uuid

fix.summary: Change the type with expand and contract instead of rewriting the table in place:

steps.title: Add user_id_new with the new type
steps.code: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN user_id_new bigint;

steps.title: Write to both columns and backfill user_id_new in batches
Read from user_id_new, then drop user_id and rename user_id_new

findings.title: Renaming column "users.users" breaks running code
findings.why: During a rolling deploy, instances running the previous release still query "users". Those queries fail as soon as this migration runs.

statement.sql: ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN users TO username

fix.summary: Rename in three deploys with expand and contract:

steps.title: Add username, write to both columns and backfill it
Read from username and stop writing users
